phronesis.role: Solo project: product, design and engineering
phronesis.intro: Phronesis is a neutral civic platform for France. It cross-references Assemblée nationale and Sénat open data so citizens can follow bills, votes and their representatives, then form their own opinion.
phronesis.challenge: Parliamentary data is public but close to unreadable: thousands of bills, tens of thousands of amendments and millions of individual votes, spread across two chambers. Most tools that make it readable also tell you what to think.
phronesis.approach: I built Phronesis around one rule: understand before you judge. The interface never scores anyone, never recommends a vote and never uses red or green for “for” and “against”. Every AI summary sits next to the official text, and a public methodology page explains every calculation.

hemicycle.title: A living hemicycle
hemicycle.body: A custom SVG hemicycle draws each chamber in official group colours. Hovering a group dims the others, every arc links to that group's page, and each vote page redraws the chamber seat by seat.

compass.title: The Boussole values quiz
compass.body: 19 dilemmas score answers on about ten value axes instead of a single left–right line. The profile stays in the browser or syncs to an account, and “Résonance” compares it with a bill's footprint using cosine similarity.

neutral.title: Designed for trust
neutral.body: A black, white and single-yellow “Carnet” style with square corners. Vote colours are deliberately monochrome, AI text is labelled and always shown beside its source, and motion respects reduced-motion settings.

cache.title: Cheap to run, fast to read
cache.body: AI only runs in offline batch jobs, never at request time. A tag-based Next.js data cache survives deployments and the weekly import clears it, so the database rarely has to wake up.

seo.title: Built to be shared
seo.body: Every page has its own metadata, canonical URL and JSON-LD. Per-route sitemaps and Open Graph images generated for each bill and vote keep links readable wherever they are posted.

shots.vote: A Senate vote, redrawn seat by seat
shots.bill: A bill: plain-language summary beside the official text
shots.compass: The Boussole: dilemmas instead of a left–right score
shots.groups: Parliamentary groups and their share of seats

phronesis.outcome: Live at phronesis-france.com and open source under the MIT licence, with weekly data imports and monthly AI jobs running on GitHub Actions.

pluclair.role: Solo project: product, design and engineering
pluclair.intro: Pluclair is a free personal-finance app for France: income, spending, savings and investments in one calm ledger, on the web and Android, for individuals and couples.
pluclair.challenge: Budget apps either need full access to your bank or drift away from reality within weeks. Pluclair had to stay accurate without connecting to anyone's bank, and handle French specifics: tax rules, regulated savings, PEA and CTO accounts, property and loans.
pluclair.approach: Each month you type in the real closing balance from your bank, and Pluclair reconciles the month against it. Spending you never recorded shows up as a measured gap instead of a silent error. The interface, “The Quiet Ledger”, stays dark and still so the only bright thing on screen is the figure that matters.

ask.title: A chat that checks its own numbers
ask.body: Ask Pluclair answers by calling 11 tools on your real data. Any amount in its answer that the tools never returned gets a dotted underline, so an invented number is visible at a glance. Users bring their own model key.

statements.title: A statement reader that balances to the cent
statements.body: It reads CSV in every French bank's flavour, XLSX and ODS, OFX and QIF, CAMT, MT940, CFONB and PDF, then checks the lines against the statement's own opening and closing balances.

light.title: Lit from behind
light.body: A coloured light glows behind every screen under a slow WebGL veil, with frosted cards on top and a single orange accent. The orb logo is pure CSS, so it costs no JavaScript.

couples.title: A shared space for couples
couples.body: A shared space owns records the way a person does, protected by Postgres row-level security, with each partner's share and a running balance between them.

year.title: Your year, as a story
year.body: An end-of-year recap told in story-style cards, each one exportable as a shareable image.

pluclair.outcome: Live at pluclair.com with a read-only demo account. One pnpm monorepo ships the Next.js web app and the Expo Android app from the same domain code and the same Supabase backend.

mip.role: Lead, design and frontend engineering at QuantCube Technology
mip.intro: The Macro Intelligence Platform delivers daily macroeconomic nowcasts to institutional analysts: GDP, inflation, trade, ports, pollution, urban traffic and more, built from alternative data. I led its complete rebuild, from the design system to the architecture.
mip.challenge: The previous platform had grown one copied folder per data module: 33 of them, around 640 files and 80,000 lines of near-identical code. Every new module meant another copy, and every design change had to be made 33 times.
mip.approach: I replaced the copies with one config-driven engine. Each module is now a single defineModule() configuration describing its data, filters, views and exports. One route renders any module, and the same config feeds the menu, dashboards and exports. Around it I built a token-driven design system with a real dark mode and a phone layout of its own.
mip.notice: The platform is private, so the visuals here are redrawn diagrams, not screenshots. They contain no client data.

engine.title: One engine, 32 modules
engine.body: Modules are declared, not coded. Adding one now takes a config, translation keys and tests, instead of a new folder of pages, stores and server code.

views.title: Eight ways to read a series
views.body: Charts, tables and six kinds of maps (regional, tension, heatmap, traffic, city and sites), all driven by the same config, with exports to CSV, Excel, JSON and image.

system.title: A token-driven design system
system.body: 228 design tokens, WCAG AA contrast, a motion scale and a real dark mode. Switching theme plays a circular reveal with the View Transitions API, and chart colours come from the same tokens so ECharts always matches the interface.

phone.title: Built for phones too
phone.body: On desktop a “notch” tab bar hangs from the app frame, with a pill that slides under the active tab. On phones it becomes a bottom bar that hides on scroll, with draggable bottom sheets for filters.

horizon.title: A sign-in worth the wait
horizon.body: The login page draws a planet horizon on a 2D canvas: a turning Blue Marble Earth, a rising sun and 1,800 stars in dark mode, a grey globe with red data flows in light mode. It holds still when reduced motion is on.

performance.title: Fast by default
performance.body: ECharts, MapLibre, the editor and the export tools only load when a page needs them, and each route ships its own chunk. ECharts is trimmed to the five chart types the app actually uses.

metrics.files: module code files compared with the old platform

mip.outcome: The rebuilt platform runs on TanStack Start, with architecture layers enforced by dependency-cruiser, 611 Vitest tests, and English and French throughout.
